{{Short description|American chemistry professor}}
'''Paul J. Hergenrother''' is an American chemist and the Kenneth L. Rinehart Jr. Endowed Chair in Natural Products chemistry at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Paul J. Hergenrother {{!}} Chemistry at Illinois |url=https://chemistry.illinois.edu/hergenro |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=chemistry.illinois.edu}}</ref> His research focuses on the development of organic small molecules with novel biological properties such as [[enzyme inhibitor]]s and activators, [[Chemotherapy|chemotherapeutics]], and [[Antibiotic|antibacterial]] agents. In 2008 Hergenrother was awarded the [[Eli Lilly Award in Biological Chemistry]].

== Education ==
Hergenrother attended college at [[University of Notre Dame]]. In 1999, Hergenrother earned his PhD in chemistry from the [[University of Texas at Austin|University of Texas]], where he worked in the lab of Professor [[Stephen F. Martin]].

== Career and research ==
From 1999 to 2001, Hergenrother completed an [[American Cancer Society]] postdoctoral fellowship at [[Harvard University]] in the lab of Professor [[Stuart Schreiber]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kuruvilla |first1=Finny G. |last2=Shamji |first2=Alykhan F. |last3=Sternson |first3=Scott M. |last4=Hergenrother |first4=Paul J. |last5=Schreiber |first5=Stuart L. |date=2002 |title=Dissecting glucose signalling with diversity-oriented synthesis and small-molecule microarrays |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/416653a |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=416 |issue=6881 |pages=653–657 |doi=10.1038/416653a |pmid=11948353 |bibcode=2002Natur.416..653K |s2cid=4424969 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2001, Hergenrother became a faculty member in the department of chemistry at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]]. In the spring of 2020, he led the team at the University of Illinois [[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois|that developed a saliva test for SARS-CoV-2]],<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Peplow |first1=Mark |last2=C |first2=special to |last3=EN |date=2025-01-21 |title=How one university built a COVID-19 screening system |url=https://cen.acs.org/biological-chemistry/infectious-disease/one-university-built-COVID-19/98/i42 |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Chemical & Engineering News |language=en}}</ref> a test that was widely used throughout the covid-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cotti |first=Sol |title=How U. of I.
